title: blessed/release-receipt/v1
description: A normalized, locally-validated record of the producer's GitHub Release. It supplies the RELEASE-PUBLICATION FACT — published_at — and provenance binding. It is NOT cryptographic authority over the candidate: candidate authenticity comes from its detached signature and its exact Release/tag binding, never from this receipt. It exists so the renderer never reads a clock and never calls the network: published_at is a stable recorded fact, produced by a credentialed fetch zone outside the pure renderer. Recreating a Release with a changed database id, tag, resolved SHA, or published_at is a CONFLICT, not a replay.

release_id.description: GitHub Release DATABASE identity. A deleted-and-recreated Release under the same tag has a different id, which must read as a conflict rather than a replay.

draft.description: Must be false. A draft Release is not a durable candidate store.

published_at.description: CANONICAL RELEASE PUBLICATION TIME, in UTC with a literal Z. This is the ONLY source of a rendered published_at. It is deliberately NOT candidate.created_at, which DocSort derives from the source commit date: for v0.4.3 created_at is 2026-08-13T01:02:56Z (commit 86e5a3f) while the Release published at 2026-08-13T01:24:49Z. Reusing created_at would publish one fact under another fact's name.
